Hi Alex / Olivia —

Thanks for the context — quick answers and a short checklist to help your networking team evaluate options. I've attached a simple diagram and the Redwood VPC checklist.

Short answers: 
- We support both VPC peering (AWS & GCP) and AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint service).
  - VPC peering: straight routing, slightly lower latency, requires route propagation and compatible CIDRs (no overlapping).
  - PrivateLink: works well to avoid exposing public IPs and simplifies IP allowlisting (traffic goes through the endpoint); slightly more setup on your side (endpoint ENIs) but often preferred for stricter security models.
- IP allowlist: if you use PrivateLink, you typically do not need to open outbound IP ranges to Redwood's public endpoints — connectivity stays in the private network. For peering, we will need the VPC CIDR(s) and any specific subnets you intend to use for peering routes.

Technical checklist (high level): 
- Cloud provider: AWS (us-west-2) — confirm
- VPC CIDR(s) and preferred subnets for peering or endpoint placement
- Do you require cross-account peering or a shared-services account setup?
- TLS: TLS 1.2+ required on all connections; port 443 (HTTPS) for API traffic.
- KMS: If you plan to use customer-managed keys for data at rest, provide KMS ARN and access role details.
- Audit/logging: we can forward request logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or ship to S3—let us know preference.
- Firewall rules: inbound only for PrivateLink (none to public); for peering add appropriate routes and allow 443.

Attachments: [Attachment: networking-diagram.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)]

Proposed next step: 30-min network breakout with your infra and our SEs to map CIDRs and agree on peering vs PrivateLink. I'm available Wed 7/14 at 10:00am or Thu 7/15 at 9:00am PT — whichever works for your team.

If you can share a contact for procurement/security, we'll send the short questionnaire and an initial SOW estimate (separate doc) to help procurement size Dedicated vs Private VPC pricing.
